* A `profiling_answer` event is recorded each time an answer is submitted to a profiling question.

params.name: offset
params.description: Offsets the starting number of events to return. Used for pagination in conjunction with the limit query.

params.name: order
params.description: Used to sort and order the results in ascending or descending order. The value can be `asc` for sorting the results by `_id` in an ascending order, or `desc` for sorting the results by `date` and `_id` in a descending order.

params.name: actions
params.description: A legacy field consisting of comma separated list of actions to filters the type of returned Antavo events.

params.name: action
params.description:
The events history can be filtered by submitted event actions using operators. Refer to [API events](/docs/api-events) and [internal events](/docs/internal-events) lists. 
This filter query can be used in conjunction with [operators](/docs/pagination-filtering-and-ordering#query-operators). The filter should be submitted as a parameter in the following format: `field.operator(optional)=value`.

Filtering of events containing a `transaction_id` is also possible. This requires the action query to contain all related events and for an additional query using `properties.transaction_id`.
Example: 
`action.in=checkout,checkout_accept&properties.transaction_id.in=c078c162-88af-4369-89a4-408958a8cb75`. 
These combined filters can also use [filtering operators](/docs/pagination-filtering-and-ordering#query-operators). 
The `transaction_id` field in any custom event must be set as filterable.

params.name: date
params.description:
The events history can be filtered by a specific date. Specific start and/or end dates can be stated by using multiple operators (e.g., `date.gt=2020-01-01&date.lt=2022-02-01`).
The UTC timezone should be considered when sending the request.

params.name: points_only
params.description: Filter to only show non-zero points events (events that award or subtract points).

params.name: references
params.description: Include the ID and name of any associated challenges/rewards in the response.

items.docs:

params.name: timestamp.lt
params.description: Filter events with timestamp less than the specified value.

params.name: timestamp.gte
params.description: Filter events with timestamp greater than or equal to the specified value.

params.name: timestamp.lte

params.description: Limits the number of events returned in one response. Other values are accessible by pagination made accessible via the offset.

params.name: offset
params.description: Offsets the starting number of events to return. Used for pagination in conjunction with the limit query.

params.name: order
params.description: Used to sort and order the results in ascending or descending order. The value can be `asc` for sorting the results by `_id` in an ascending order, or `desc` for sorting the results by `date` and `_id` in a descending order.

items.docs:
This endpoint returns all events for all customers that match the specified datetime timestamp query.
The returned object contains the total number of matching events and an array of every matching event.	

The datetime filter accepts the following operators and can be combined to generate a time window:

* `gt` - greater than

* `lt` - less than 

* `gte` - greater than or equal

 * `lte` - less than or equal

 The timestamp filter must be in ISODate format. Example: ``timestamp.gt=2023-01-05``

info.name: Customers
Verify credentials provided during registration

items.docs:
This endpoint is used to confirm registration.

A successful verification will change the status of the customer to `active` and enable them to log in and engage with the loyalty program. Failure will leave the customer in an `inactive` status.

The verification process occurs using a token.

This requires the Custom login module with the verification option enabled (disabled by default).

info.name: Create a new customer with log-in credentials

items.docs:
This endpoint creates customer within Antavo according to the specified opt-in parameters stated in the body. 

This interface is primarily used as a customer-driven registration process which also generates login credentials, enabling the new customer to log into Antavo systems. This endpoint complements the [opt-in](https://developers.antavo.com/docs/api-events#opt_in) event.

info.name: Log in a specific customer to Antavo

items.docs:
This endpoint logs the specified customer into Antavo and a successful login returns the customer object.

The username attribute can be specified in the Antavo Management UI from any available profile attribute.
The customer ID can then be accessed and used for subsequent calls using Antavo Display API endpoints.

A successful log-in will also create a ``daily_login`` event for the customer.
This event will only be written once to the customer's event stream per calendar day.

info.name: Request a new password for Antavo login

items.docs:
A forgotten password can be reset through this endpoint.
The username can be set in the Customer login module in the Management UI and can be any customer profile attribute.
The `url` string is a URL which can be extended with the reset token.

info.name: Reset the password of the current customer

items.docs:
This provides a customer interface for changing a password. The token is captured from the link provided by the password reset email. A simple check is provided to ensure that the two passwords match.
This requires the Custom login module to be enabled.
